# Maximum Support Material

Estimated percentage of surface area requiring support material.

<figure markdown="span">
![Maximum Support Material: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/max-support-material-light.svg#only-light){ width="640" }
![Maximum Support Material: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/max-support-material-dark.svg#only-dark){ width="640" }
<figcaption>Percentage of surface area that requires support structures.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Where it applies

| Process | Criticality |
| :-- | :-- |
| [FDM](../../reference/processes/fdm-3d-printing.md) | Medium |

## Values

**Aim for** is what to design for; crossing it gives a warning. **At most** is the hard limit; crossing it gives an error. See [aim for and limits](../../concepts/aim-for-and-limits.md).

Criticality in this process: **Medium** ([what this means](../../concepts/criticality.md)).

| Material | Aim for | At most | Source |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Default** | 15% | 30% | Not yet sourced |

Every other material uses the Default values: PLA, PLA-CF (Carbon Fiber), PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU (Flexible), PA, PA-CF (Carbon Fiber), PC.

## Messages

What the results panel says about a finding. You can rewrite these in the Process Library; the words in `{braces}` are filled in for each finding.

!!! warning "Warning"

    Support coverage `{measured}` exceeds the recommended `{target}`. A large supported region adds print time, uses extra filament, and leaves surface marks where supports are removed.
!!! failure "Error"

    Support coverage `{measured}` exceeds the `{limit}` limit. Extensive support material increases the risk of failed supports, difficult removal, and scarred surfaces. Reorient the part or redesign overhanging features to reduce dependence on supports.
| Placeholder | Replaced with |
| :-- | :-- |
| `{measured}` | The measured value, with its unit |
| `{target}` | The rule's "Aim for" value |
| `{limit}` | The rule's "At most" value |
